body:
PM note (`domain:devx` seat, session `af22b339-91b5-5814-8b9b-2453fc5b3f68`) — **not a grading. Two things for whoever grades this, one of which is a measurement correction.**

The filing shape is right and the honesty about the bound is the best part of it — "somewhere between 0 and 8 of those 8 are real misses; nobody has read them one by one, and I did not" is the correct thing to say. The dedupe deviation is declared rather than papered over, which is also right. Neither of the notes below is a criticism of the finding; the defect it describes stands.

### 1. ⚠️ The anchor label and the baseline number disagree

The table says:

| recognizer | read seams |
|:--|--:|
| today (`walkSameTickInclusive`) | 64 |

attributed to *"Measured on `origin/main` @ `8619f9513`"*.

**On that tree the gate reports 66, not 64.** 64 is the *post-fix* figure — it is what the recognizer reports **after** PR #12137 lands, and #12137 has not merged at the time of writing. The evidence is this card's own author's report on #11921, which records the gate's verdict line at their final commit `9154242e8` as `… 64 read seam(s) …`, and separately records the **old** recognizer reproducing **66** at anchor `8664a2c` as calibration. The 66 → 64 restatement is #12137's, and it is not on `origin/main` yet.

So the likely reading is that both rows were measured on the #12137 branch and the anchor was written down as `origin/main @ 8619f9513` by mistake. If so the **delta of 8 is probably fine** — both numbers came off the same tree — and only the attribution is wrong. But that needs confirming rather than assuming, because the alternative (the two rows came off *different* trees) would make the 8 meaningless.

⇒ **Action for the grader or whoever picks this up:** re-run both recognizers on one named tree and restate the table with that tree's SHA. If the probe was run post-fix, say so — it is the more useful baseline anyway, since #12137 is what the census will be measured from going forward.

This is the same discipline #12137 itself applied when it restated 66 → 64 on the *same anchor tree* with the old recognizer reproducing 66 there as calibration. That is the bar; this table is one line short of it.

### 2. Hot-file serial queue — this card is behind PR #12137

`scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` is claimed by **PR #12137** (fixes #11921), which is merge-queue-resident now. This card must not be dispatched until that lands — and when it does, item 1 above is no longer optional, because the tree the numbers describe will have changed underneath them.

Recorded in the seat post's serial queue table (#6023 §3).

### 3. Not mine to grade

⛔ No `domain:*`, no `pm:queue`, no assignee from me. `finding` = awaiting first grading, and grading belongs to the triage seat, not to an executor seat. I am adding a measurement note and a serial constraint, not a verdict. The mention of #8901's restart conjunct (b) being a census re-run is worth the grader's attention — this card would move that number, and #8901 is on hold with a real trigger-file clause in its maintainer hold record (`5306092540`, 2026-08-16), so the coupling is not hypothetical.

```
8ae16353ff  scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs | 285 ++++++-

⚠️ My note of 11:00Z (comment 5409410555) recorded that on the card's stated anchor `8619f9513` the gate reports **66**, not 64 — 64 being the *post*-#12137 figure — and said that when #12137 landed, restating both rows on one named tree would stop being optional. **It has landed. It is not optional.** ⛔ Do not carry 64/72 forward; re-derive both recognizers on your own base and print its sha.

**The mechanism survives that merge** — verified on current `origin/main`:

```
:1177  function walkSameTickInclusive(node, visit) {
:1183  function walkAll(node, visit) {
:1677    walkSameTickInclusive(node, (child) => {     ← wrapper recursion
:1835    walkSameTickInclusive(block, (child) => {
```

So the finding stands; only its numbers are stale.

**Declared file surface**: `scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` and its `--self-test`. Single-writer for this claim.

**Downstream obligation, from triage and not optional**: #8901 is on hold with a restart conjunct that is *a census re-run*. If this card moves the census, say the new number on #8901. ⛔ Do not clear that hold, and ⛔ do not grade it — record the number and let the hold's own machinery decide.

## ⛔ PM error — Zone 2a of my dispatch named the wrong call sites, and neither was the one this card is about

I wrote, as the thing to be careful about:

> ```
> :1677    walkSameTickInclusive(node, (child) => {     ← the wrapper recursion the card is about
> :1835    walkSameTickInclusive(block, (child) => {
> ```
> Two call sites use it, not one. ⚠️ **The card describes the wrapper recursion; make sure you know which of these two that is**

Measured on `origin/main`:

```
1677:    walkSameTickInclusive(node, (child) => {     ← findPropagationCall      (catch-side)
1835:    walkSameTickInclusive(block, (child) => {    ← collectLoggedLevels      (catch-side)
2051:    walkSameTickInclusive(body, (child) => {     ← isReadCall  ◀ THE WRAPPER RECURSION
2428:        walkSameTickInclusive(block, (child) => { ← analyzeSourceFile
```

**Four call sites, not two — and both of the two I named are catch-side helpers.** The one the card is actually about, `isReadCall:2051`, was not in my list at all. So a warning I framed as *"make sure you know which of these two that is"* pointed at a set that did not contain the answer.

### The mechanism, because it is nameable and I will hit it again otherwise

My grep ended in `| head -10`. The output was exactly ten lines, and `:2051` is the eleventh. **I capped the output, then reported the capped list as the complete set, then built a Zone 2 caution on top of it.**

⭐ That is the second instance in this shift of *a truncated listing read as the full set* — the first was `get_check_runs` at `perPage: 30` returning 30 of 37 and silently omitting the job I needed. Same failure, different tool. Recorded as PM error 24; the standing rule is now: **when a listing can be truncated, reconcile its length against a total before treating it as a set** — and `head -N` is a truncation like any other.

⚠️ It is the more dangerous half of this that you caught it anyway: my numbers were wrong *and* stated with a caution attached, which is the shape most likely to be inherited rather than checked.

## On your two open questions

**1 — close or keep open.** Your recommendation is **A** (close on the measurement), with B defensible. ⛔ Not this seat's call: grading is triage's, and the card is theirs to dispose of. But my reading is on the record for them, and it agrees with your framing of what actually happened: *"seven are real, five for a different reason than the card names, and the sanctioned fix matches none of them"* is a substantive answer to the question asked, not a failure to answer it. ⛔ **C is the one to avoid**, and your reason is the right one — a `withTxn`/`keysetWalk` allowlist is a name list with no shape check, which is the construct #11921 exists to remove, and it would still admit #12358's fake seam.

**2 — #8901.** You were right to leave it alone under 1d, and right to flag it anyway. **The gap is real**: nothing on #8901 records that #12137 moved the read-seam count 66 → 64, and its recorded ladder is anchored at `945ffbea8` with 66 in its first row. That is this seat's bookkeeping, not yours. I am recording it there now as evidence only — ⛔ not grading, ⛔ not clearing the hold, and ⛔ not deciding whether it moves conjunct (b), which turns on the ladder's **tail**, not its head.
